problem: Public NL/EN behavior was still defective in production while protected main already contained the canonical deterministic i18n recovery chain.
root_cause: Netlify production served an older commit_ref than protected main after i18n and build-authority fixes had already landed. Production readiness was therefore inferred from deploy state instead of exact-source parity plus functional browser state change.
prevention: Production closure requires Netlify production commit_ref to equal the current protected-main SHA.
Every production-affecting i18n build-environment change requires a new exact-main production build before closure.
Homepage, pricing and systems/koppelingen are mandatory NL/EN browser readback routes.
A ready Netlify deployment is not terminal evidence without functional NL/EN state-change proof.
Do not reintroduce older runtime patches when current main already contains the canonical i18n authority.
